articles.title: Why Two Man Utd Talents Have Joined Arsenal in the Last Two Days
articles.excerpt: The Gunners have deliberately recruited several young players with first-team ambitions.
articles.content:
This weekend, Arsenal signed James Scanlon from Manchester United on Saturday and then announced the capture of Habeeb Ogunneye, also from the Red Devils, on Sunday.

It is part of a targeted approach from the Gunners this summer to strengthen at the academy level, with five such players recruited in the last five days alone.

Scanlon, who turns 20 next month, and Ogunneye, 21 in November, are talents who will hope to join on the fringes of the first team and soon make that breakthrough. Neither ever made a first-team appearance for Manchester United, although both did get on the senior bench and both gained first-team experience in the EFL League Two during loans last season.

It is a reversal of the transfer that saw an 18-year-old Ayden Heaven leave Arsenal for Manchester United in January 2025 in the hope of a clearer pathway. The center back has since played 25 senior matches and appears to have a bright future, which so far vindicates the decision to switch clubs in the hope of furthering his career.

Arsenal Sign Left-Wing Prospect

Scanlon was born and raised in England’s East Midlands, having been in Derby County’s academy before moving to Manchester aged 14, but appears to be motivated by Arsenal’s recent Premier League success and the upward trajectory of the club.

“I think you can see where the club’s at, [it’s] really positive and I think it’s only going to get better,” the teenager told Arsenal’s in-house media.

“You can see that everyone here is hungrier for more, hungrier to get better and I think that’s something I believe I can add to and want to be a part of as well.”

With Arsenal struggling to recruit another left winger this summer but in the process of selling Gabriel Martinelli to Al Hilal, there is potentially a direct path into the first team for Scanlon, who plays on the left or as a No. 10. The youngster, who already has 24 international caps for Gibraltar, describes himself as a “creative player” who likes to “score goals, assist.”

Arsenal’s Recent Youth Development Stands Out

Ogunneye is originally from London and so has a clear family connection to the city, although his association with Manchester United lasted 15 years—most of his young life.

The defender is specifically a right back and said upon joining the club that he hopes Arsenal’s production line will serve him as it has done others in recent years.

"When I heard [Arsenal] were interested in me, I said to my agents it’s a no-brainer,” Ogunneye explained. “Seeing all the young players that are coming through as well, I just wanted to come straight away. I just wanted to be part of that group, and win games together. It’s good playing with good players, good defenders; it’s only going to better you.”

Myles Lewis-Skelly, Max Dowman and Ethan Nwaneri have all made the jump from Arsenal’s Hale End academy to the first team in the past few seasons. Bukayo Saka was also only 18 years old when he started regularly playing for the senior squad in 2019.

In Ogunneye’s position there initially appears to be more immediate competition than Scanlon might face, with Jurriën Timber and Ben White the primary right backs. Cristhian Mosquera and Ezri Konsa can also play the position, although both are seen as center backs first.

It’s worth noting, however, that Timber is currently sidelined and has been injured for a cumulative 443 days since joining in 2023. White has also often been linked with an exit since losing his starting place, and Ogunneye might not be that far away from an opportunity. 

Jamie Spencer is a writer and editor for SI FC. Jamie grew up in Manchester, England, in the 1990s and fell in love with the game at the same time as the Premier League was taking off. With more than a decade of experience behind him in sports media, he specializes in Manchester United and the overall Premier League, still living in England’s north-west soccer hotbed. Jamie is also an expert on the women’s game and enjoys old school nostalgia, telling stories from soccer’s rich history and culture.

articles.title: Amazon’s “House of the Dragon Meets Shadow and Bone” Show Will Be Its New King of Fantasy
articles.excerpt: Amazon is one of the best streaming services for fantasy, and one upcoming show seems destined to cement itself as the king of the genre.
articles.content:
In the wake of Game of Thrones, Prime Video is the streaming service that has the strongest fantasy offerings — well, if we're not counting HBO Max and its spin-offs, anyway. Despite multiple platforms rushing to capitalize on the success of the Song of Ice and Fire adaptation, few have succeeded in creating epic franchises on the same scale. Netflix's attempts with The Witcher and Shadow and Bone are not much to brag about, and Apple TV is leaning more into sci-fi right now (though its take on Brandon Sanderson's Cosmere will properly put it in the fantasy game).

Prime Video has multiple original fantasy series in its library, each boasting varying degrees of quality and success. The most notable is The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, which is an absolute spectacle in terms of production — but more divisive as a J.R.R. Tolkien adaptation, and feels like it's still finding its stride. The Wheel of Time is a contender that took its final bow, with Prime Video canceling it after Season 3. And The Legend of Vox Machina is probably Prime Video's most promising addition to the category to date, but it remains underrated among mainstream audiences.

Needless to say, it's hard to crown a new king of fantasy in Game of Thrones' wake, or even just among Amazon's productions. An upcoming series may clear things up, though, claiming that title with its "House of the Dragon meets Shadow and Bone" storyline.

The 'Fourth Wing' Show Is Poised to Become Prime Video's New King of Fantasy

It Has All the Ingredients to Become a Wider Hit

Prime Video is already ahead in the fantasy race, but the streamer isn't done releasing new projects — and one of its most exciting upcoming endeavors is Fourth Wing. Based on the viral TikTok sensation written by Rebecca Yarros, the TV show will be produced by Michael B. Jordan and his production company, Outlier Society. It will follow Violet Sorrengail as she embarks on a quest to become a dragon rider at Basgiath War College, despite spending her entire life training to become a scholar. Violet's journey includes trials, magic, military conspiracies, and obviously, dragons — all things that make it well worth going on with her.

With so many great ingredients for a fantasy story, Fourth Wing feels destined to become a wider hit once it arrives on Prime Video. There's a reason it's appealing to longtime fantasy readers and newcomers in book form, and that's something the TV series should be able to replicate. The charming characters, timely themes, and high stakes — and did I mention dragons? — make it all too easy to immerse yourself in. The show will cement itself as Prime Video's top fantasy title just because of how popular and accessible it is. There's also the fact that it meshes two very different series, offering something for multiple brands of fantasy lovers.

'Fourth Wing' Will Be "House of the Dragon Meets Shadow and Bone" in the Best Way

It Features Strengths From Both Fantasy Series

Fourth Wing is likely to dominate Prime Video, but it's a great blend of two shows from other platforms: House of the Dragon and Shadow and Bone. The House of the Dragon comparison feels obvious. Although Fourth Wing isn't as concerned with succession and power grabs as the Game of Thrones spin-off, it has all the dragon-riding action audiences could want. Its dragons talk, too, giving them more personality than even the best House of the Dragon creatures.

Meanwhile, Fourth Wing's romance story — complete with a shadow-wielding MMC — and military focus make it a solid choice for anyone looking to replace Shadow and Bone. The plots aren't quite the same, but they check a lot of the same boxes. They also have a similar feel, and with Shadow and Bone canceled, Fourth Wing can carry that forward. Hopefully, its range of strengths will work to its advantage, allowing it to resonate with a broader viewership. That's what fantasy needs to reach the heights of Game of Thrones, and Fourth Wing is one series that could actually pull that off.
